United States | status = In production, in service | produced = December 2015–present | number_built = 271 (Q4 2025){{cite web |last= |first= |date=February 18, 2026 |title=2025 General Aviation Aircraft Shipment Report |url=https://gama.aero/wp-content/uploads/2025-General-Aviation-Aircraft-Shipment-Report.pdf |url-status=live |publisher=General Aviation Manufacturers Association |access-date=April 30, 2026}} }} The '''Honda HA-420 HondaJet''' is a light [[business jet]] produced by the [[Honda Aircraft Company]] of [[Greensboro, North Carolina]], United States. Original concepts of the aircraft started in 1997 and were completed in 1999. It took its [[maiden flight]] on December 3, 2003, received its FAA [[type certificate]] in December 2015, and was first delivered that same month. The six- or seven-seat aircraft has a composite [[fuselage]] and an aluminum wing, and is powered by two unusually mounted [[GE Honda HF120]] turbofans, on [[Hardpoint#Pylon|pylons]] above the wing. It can cruise at {{convert|422|kn|lk=in|abbr=~}} and has a range of up to {{convert|1547|nmi|lk=in|abbr=~}}. The HondaJet has received several aeronautic design and innovation accolades. == Development == [[File:AERO Friedrichshafen 2018, Friedrichshafen (1X7A4376).jpg|thumb|The HA-420 made its first flight in 2003, and received FAA [[type certificate]] in 2015.]] Honda began to study small-sized [[business jet]]s in the late 1980s, using engines from other manufacturers. The Honda MH01 [[turboprop]] used an all-composite construction, and the [[Honda MH02]] was fabricated and assembled at [[Mississippi State University#Accolades|Mississippi State University's Raspet Flight Research Laboratory]] in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The MH02 was a prototype using carbon fiber/epoxy composite materials and was the first all-composite light business jet to fly.{{Cite web |title=Raspet Flight Research Laboratory: History/Honda Jet |url=http://www.ae.msstate.edu/rfrl/pages/hondajet.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030907012515/http://www.ae.msstate.edu/rfrl/pages/hondajet.html |archive-date=September 7, 2003 |access-date=December 23, 2010 |publisher=Ae.msstate.edu}} Flight testing on the MH02 continued through 1996, after which the aircraft was shipped to Japan.{{Cite web |title=Aircraft N3079N Data |url=https://www.airport-data.com/aircraft/N3079N.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190217093425/http://www.airport-data.com/aircraft/N3079N.html |archive-date=February 17, 2019 |access-date=August 2, 2020 |website=airport-data.com}} Lead designer and company founder [[Michimasa Fujino]] began sketching the HondaJet in 1997, and the concept was solidified in 1999. A similar over-wing engine configuration was used in the 1970s on the [[VFW-Fokker 614]], but had limited the aircraft's speed due to interference between the engine and the wing.{{Cite tech report |first=Steven H. |last=Berguin |author2=Sudharshan Ashwin Renganathan |author3=Jai Ahuja |author4=Mengzhen Chen |author5=Christian Perron |author6=Jimmy Tai |author7=Dimitri N. Mavris |title=CFD Study of an Over-Wing Nacelle Configuration |number=1853/60464 |institution=Georgia Institute of Technology |date=October 2018 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328223348_CFD_Study_of_an_Over-Wing_Nacelle_Configuration}} This, along with the overall commercial failure of the VFW-Fokker 614, made the over-wing configuration unpopular with aircraft designers.{{Cite book |last=Fujino |first=Michimasa |title=Fundamentals of Aircraft and Airship Design, Volume 2 – Airship Design and Case Studies |date=2013 |publisher=American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics |isbn=978-1-60086-898-6 |editor-last=Carichner |editor-first=Grant E. |pages=615–647 |chapter=Case Study 4: HondaJet |editor-last2=Nicolai |editor-first2=Leland M.}}{{Cite web |last=Shòu |first=Tuó |date=February 10, 2018 |title=Běntián kāi mài de shuāng fā pēnqì shì fēijī, wèi shà bǎ fādòngjī dǐng zài jī yì shàng?——Zhuānfǎng HondaJet shèjì shī téngyě dào gé |script-title=zh: 本田开卖的双发喷气式飞机，为啥把发动机顶在机翼上？——专访HondaJet设计师藤野道格 |trans-title=Honda has Started to Sell a Twin-Engine Light Jet, but why did they put the Engines on top of the Wings? The HondaJet's engines are positioned in such a way that the airflow over the wing is superimposed with the airflow around the engine to minimize [[wave drag]] at high speed.{{Cite journal |last=Fujino |first=Michimasa |author-link=Michimasa Fujino |date=Nov–Dec 2003 |title=Wave-Drag Characteristics of an Over-the-Wing Nacelle Business-Jet Configuration |url=https://www.hondajet.com/Content/pdf/tech_papers/Journal_of_Aircraft_Vol40_No6_P1177_P1184_Wave_Drag_OTWEM.pdf |journal=[[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics#Journals|Journal of Aircraft]] |volume=40 |issue=6 |pages=1177–1184 |doi=10.2514/2.7207 |access-date=August 26, 2020 |archive-date=August 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220829145941/https://www.hondajet.com/ |url-status=live }} The HondaJet designer calls this "favorable interference." This configuration not only eliminated the problems associated with earlier over-wing engine mounts, but actually reduced wave drag compared to a conventional rear-fuselage mounted configuration. OTWEM configuration is often named the most unusual feature of the HondaJet. The nose and wing are designed for [[laminar flow]], and the main fuselage has a constant profile, making an eventual stretch easier. The combination of engine placement, wing and fuselage was achieved using [[Riemann solver|computer simulations]] and [[wind tunnel]]s.{{Cite journal |last=Fujino |first=Michimasa |author-link=Michimasa Fujino |date=May–June 2005 |title=Design and Development of the HondaJet |url=http://www.hondajet.com/Content/pdf/tech_papers/Journal_of_Aircraft_Vol42_No3_P755_P764_HondaJet.pdf |journal=[[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics#Journals|Journal of Aircraft]] |volume=42 |issue=3 |pages=755–764, 759 |doi=10.2514/1.12268 |access-date=March 28, 2015 |archive-date=August 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220829154514/https://www.hondajet.com/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite magazine |last=Garrison |first=Peter |date=December 2006 |title=Technicalities |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LIyBivex-C4C&pg=PA84 |magazine=Flying |page=83}} The HondaJet has a retractable [[tricycle landing gear]] with both main and nose landing gear single-wheeled. Jet It CEO Glenn Gonzales indicated that Honda's customer support was "grossly inadequate" and announced plans in the autumn of 2022 to sell its fleet of HondaJets and buy [[Embraer Phenom 300]]s instead. As a result, Honda launched a lawsuit against Jet It in December 2022, for an alleged breach of contract in reselling one of its Honda aircraft, although the lawsuit was subsequently settled out of court. The HondaJet Owners and Pilots Association also called for a safety stand-down and meeting for its members, as a result of eight HondaJet accidents in the previous 12 months.{{Cite web |last=Phelps |first=Mark |date=May 23, 2023 |title=Fractional Operator Grounds Its HondaJet Fleet; Honda Rebuts |url=https://www.avweb.com/aviation-news/fractional-operator-grounds-its-hondajet-fleet-honda-rebuts/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230524114126/https://www.avweb.com/aviation-news/fractional-operator-grounds-its-hondajet-fleet-honda-rebuts/ |archive-date=May 24, 2023 |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=AVweb}} The first fatal accident involving a HondaJet happened on November 5, 2024, when an HA-420 with registration N57HP overran the runway on takeoff and crashed into a vehicle on the adjacent road at [[Falcon Field (Arizona)|Falcon Field]] in [[Mesa, Arizona]].
